title: Give Your Agent a Computer — Nico Albanese, Vercel
talk_summary: Nico Albanese demos building an AI SDK 6 tool-loop agent with a persistent named Vercel sandbox, a single bash tool, and a memories.md file injected into the system prompt each run. He argues the core 2026 agent primitives are runtime, tools, and a computer/file system, and shares context-engineering lessons from a coding agent he runs daily (sub-agents, handoff, avoiding compaction).

takeaways.what_they_do: Reference a sandbox by name; the platform routes to an active instance or spins one up, snapshots the filesystem on inactivity timeout, and restores state on the next request so it feels like the same machine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every sandbox has a name and then every sandbox can have sessions

takeaways.technique: Single bash tool instead of many bespoke tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent one bash tool (description + input schema + execute) and let it compose ls/grep/find/python itself rather than defining many narrow tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we feel very strongly that bash is all you need in a lot of cases

takeaways.technique: Plan file + research dir as external scratchpad
takeaways.what_they_do: Instruct the agent to write an objective+plan file at session start, then follow it to a T, checking items off, with a separate research directory, so the objective is re-read each step instead of decaying in a long context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create this plan file and in that plan file was the objective right at the top

takeaways.technique: Avoid compaction; use sub-agents and handoff
takeaways.what_they_do: Skip lossy summarization/compaction (which invalidates the input cache), instead offload independent work to sub-agents that return ~500-token summaries, and give the agent a handoff tool to start a fresh thread.
takeaways.numbers: 104-minute run, 316 tool calls, 29 files, 32% of context; 95% cache read ratio; sub-agent used 30k tokens, returned ~500

takeaways.what_they_do: Store memory as a file in the sandbox; a prepare-call step reads it once per run and injects it into instructions, with prompt rules to only record important facts and to save reusable scripts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: memory is a file that you store in your sandbox

takeaways.technique: Durable workflow steps per LLM step
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the agent inside a durable workflow where each LLM step maps to a workflow step that retries until it succeeds, enabling long background runs with resumable streams.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each LLM step is matched to a durable workflow step
